title: House Robber II
statement: Houses are arranged in a circle, so the first and last houses are adjacent. Return the maximum amount you can rob without robbing adjacent houses.
hints: The circle only adds one constraint: you cannot take both the first and the last house.
Run the linear robber on nums without the last house, and again on nums without the first house.
The answer is the larger of those two results. A single house is its own answer.

approaches.name: Case recursion
approaches.explanation: Branch on taking the first house.

editorial: Any optimal circular plan either excludes the first house or excludes the last house. The linear algorithm solves each of those ranges. Take the maximum. The two ranges overlap in the middle, which is allowed because the plans are alternatives, not a combination.

examples.explanation: Rob the first and third, or the second, for 4? 1+3=4 and first-last conflict. Answer 4.
